findings.F1: Inside the choppy calm profile, the 7-day excess return rises steadily across the quintiles of the 30-day return: -4.7 % (t -2.74), -2.1 %, +1.4 %, +3.2 % and +5.1 % (t 1.81). Each quintile holds only 28 to 29 grid cases, and the day-clustered slope from step 5 has t 1.35. So the tested idea's grading is visible but cannot be told from chance.
findings.F2: Inside the profile, the signed excess return per case comes mostly from one year and one window. It is +6.2 % in 2021 against +0.2 % to +1.0 % in 2018 to 2020, and +15.9 % in w18 on 13 cases. In 5 of the 11 windows it is negative. The book's Calmar failure (0.51) fits an effect that does not repeat across periods.
findings.F3: Outside the profile, the 30-day return does not grade the next 7 days. Its quintiles give -0.1 %, -3.8 % (t -3.63), -0.3 %, +2.8 % (t 2.12) and +0.4 % excess on 167 to 168 cases each, with no order between the extremes. The continuation does not carry over to rising or falling markets.
findings.F4: Where a day closes inside its own range has mixed links to what follows.
findings.F5: Several other angles show nothing that stands out once cases are clustered by day.
findings.F6: Coin returns by weekday are high on Friday and Saturday: +0.48 % (t 3.42) and +0.59 % (t 4.51) on about 1,425 coin-days each.
findings.F7: Long trades earn +3.46 % net on average (median +0.83 %, 298 trades), short trades -0.32 % (median -1.59 %, 291 trades). The weakest long-forecast quarter earns the most (+5.1 %), the strongest the least (+1.7 %). Positions do not pay more when the forecast is larger, and the shorts carry none of the book's gain.

no_ideas: Across about fifteen angles (forecast quintiles in and out of the profile, past 7-day and 1-day returns, range and relative range, close position at 1, 3 and 7 days by trend and year, volatility ratio, weekdays, trades by side, forecast and coin), no pattern holds a day-clustered t clearly above the bar such a search requires (the best are t -2.83 and 2.09). The few near it repeat ideas the profile map already holds: close near the high continuing in rising markets, next-day close-height fade, and late-week gain.
